summary:
Turn 63 responded to a side effect of last turn's F2: the scope clarification invalidated the C1 artifacts' basis, so the check is being re-executed against the current claim version.

What happened. The F2 scope clarification was applied and bumped C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector to version 2, but because a direct check's semantic inputs changed, all six of its artifacts now carry the blocker "Direct-check semantic inputs changed; execution requires re-execution" and their confirmations were withdrawn — the C1 conclusion dropped from confirmed_in_scope to investigation_lead. The other nine claims (C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C10) are unaffected and remain confirmed or bounded.

What was submitted. The C1 check is resubmitted on the same unit with the reviewed three-property plan (adoption at the resolution, the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison, agreement across replicas after the Commit broadcast) and the reviewed driven harness bytes, so a fresh execution is bound to claim version 2. No requirement, condition, predicate, prerequisite, identity or harness logic changed; the claim's obligation is identical to the version the artifacts were reviewed against, and the only difference is the scope text that now names claim C3 for the applied-state proposition — which is precisely what the F2 was for.

Lesson recorded for the remaining turns. Amending a claim's scope text is not free: it forces re-execution of every artifact whose basis includes that claim, so clarifications of this kind should be batched or avoided near the end of a run. The next step is a current-version correspondence review of the fresh execution, after which the C1 agreement finding (and the promoted-leader variant C6, which is untouched) will be confirmed again on the amended wording. No earlier observation, premise or requirement was weakened.
